subject.title: [Feature]: Capability-based permissions for skills/tools (default-deny high-risk actions)

question: What public capability taxonomy, grant storage, default-deny upgrade behavior, and enforcement boundary should OpenClaw adopt for skills/tools?
rationale: This defines a security boundary, public plugin/skill metadata, persisted grants, upgrade behavior, and audit ownership; those semantics cannot be safely inferred from current name-based policies or hook-time governance.

options.title: Approve phased core capability model
options.body: Start with schema/parser diagnostics, then add grants, pre-exposure filtering, execution-boundary checks, and audit storage behind an approved contract.

options.title: Limit to inspect-only descriptors
options.body: Add visible capability declarations without enforcement, with explicit wording that they are advisory until a later security design lands.

options.title: Keep governance plugin-owned
options.body: Treat before_tool_call governance plugins as the intended extension point and close or narrow the core item unless a missing API is identified.

recommendation.title: Approve phased core capability model
recommendation.body: Start with schema/parser diagnostics, then add grants, pre-exposure filtering, execution-boundary checks, and audit storage behind an approved contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Security posture, Gateway enforcement, and the prior human keep-open review are the main unresolved decision surfaces.
